prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies transformer/feeder circuits under approved designs/limits; observation remains separate from control/protection.
Bay Automation Controller (Juniper), comprising North Bay Controller and South Bay Controller, sequences bays, applies permissives/interlocks, produces Bay Status Digest. Breaker Control Unit executes authorized commands with interlocks; local authority prevails; remote operation requires station authority, bay selection, availability, permitted modes.
Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) independently protects its feeder using approved setting groups; produces Relay Diagnostic Note.
Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing) presents indications/communication quality, produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip; supplies no dedicated protection. Communications loss makes displays stale/unavailable; recovery requires currency verification. Station Gateway carries authorized remote communications.
Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) distributes reference time, produces Clock Drift Snapshot at configured condition; loss invokes device-specific holdover. Timing quality distinguishes synchronized/degraded/unavailable; timestamps cannot establish measurement/protection validity.
Station DC System powers protection/automation within capacity. Sequence Event Archive (Orchard), authoritative operational-event repository, preserves received records including source, event/receipt times, available quality.
Maintenance Remote Terminal permits approved maintenance without overriding local authority. Engineering Workstation controls revisions/history, produces Settings Review Receipt; access requires engineering responsibility. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) documents study-based, uniquely revisioned, coordinated changes; independent qualified review/approval precedes release. Deployment requires model/firmware compatibility, approved windows, installed-value comparison, functional checks; discrepancies block release.
Substation Supervisor confirms procedural/operational suitability, enforces authorization, escalates availability concerns. Substation Field Crew (Cinder) reviews scope/access/hazards/communications, records arrival/departure, establishes boundaries, verifies identity/position/isolation/absence of hazardous energy using approved procedures—not screens alone; sends Breaker Inspection Tag containing condition/time. Discrepancies remain unsafe until resolved; uncertainty is reported. Communications loss stops affected work under hold/escalation procedures. Completion requires personnel/tools/temporary-connection accounting and safe area.
Switching Desk Coordinator confirms switching/clearances and handback before service return. Control Room Operator verifies commanded states, coordinates access, may suspend work, evaluates field reports before automated-operation return. Automation never replaces required field verification.
